correctness.rationale: The stationary signed flip-state obeys Z' = A−1−AZ with E A<1 and admits a unique stationary law. An explicit synchronous coupling bounds its difference by 2p/[(1−p)(1−E_G e^(−κT))]. Equilibrium renewal reward and four quantitative Lipschitz error terms yield W1 ≤ Vp(2ν+4/κ)/μ for every finite-mean positive base law G. The deterministic-cycle density has explicit second and fourth moments. Rational exponential-series brackets give K4>0.0329, and 16W1<0.0329 for every L≥300. verify.py replays independent finite moment checks; it is not substituted for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-average running budget can conceal an arbitrarily rare, very long propulsion episode: time-stationary spatial laws then retain universal nonzero endpoint atoms even though the underlying interarrival law converges weakly to the ordinary clock. The quantitative W1 convergence and rigorously positive stationary fourth-cumulant counterexample establish a concrete physical failure of both weak-clock continuity and the usual negative-kurtosis intuition for harmonic telegraph confinement. This is a motivated structural/boundary result rather than an unmotivated parameter slice.
